# Long Term Vision + Goal

This project explores the most efficient ways to run a variety of AI/LLM generations on **Vulkan** using the AMD AI MAX+ 395 "Strix Halo" platform, with gfx1151 and RDNA3.5. 

Ultimately we want to be able to run these tasks:
  1. Speech to Text via Nvidia's `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`:
    * https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14128v2
  2. Text generation via Qwen's `Qwen3.8-Next-Flash`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30320v1
    * We'll need to quantise the weights once we've determined the most efficient method for the hardware
  3. Text to Speech via Hexgrad's `kokoro-82M`:
    * https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2306.07691v2
  4. Image generation via Tongyi's `z-image-turbo`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2511.22699v5
    * With this smaller model to generate in-progress previews: 
      * https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/taef1
  5. Compute embeddings via Qwen's `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05176v3

We will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these features, in Go.

1	# PIPELINE — the z-image-turbo vertical slice
2	
3	> **PARKED 2026-09-14, and this file is the record of where.** The current
4	> work is [`SPEECH.md`](SPEECH.md) — the parakeet and kokoro verticals — and
5	> this slice resumes after them. Nothing below is stale: it is the state the
6	> pipeline is in, and the three items under "Where the image budget stands"
7	> are where to pick it up. The short version: an image is **14.26 s**, the DiT
8	> is **94%** of it, and the only thing left worth more than a percent is the
9	> **quarter of the WMMA ceiling the seven projections do not reach — 2.6 s**.
10	
11	> **This file is rewritten, not appended.** It states where the pipeline is
12	> *now* and what happens next. History belongs in `TODO.md` (session
13	> handoffs) and `research/` (closed findings); if a paragraph here is about
14	> the past, it is in the wrong file. Keep it under ~200 lines — it earns a
15	> few more with each stage that closes, and loses them when a stage's detail
16	> moves to `research/`.
17	
18	**Status**: **the target is met, and the block has no layout work left in it.**
19	`go run ./cmd/zimage -prompt "..."` writes a 1024x1024 PNG in **14.3 s** —
20	tokenizer, text encoder, 34 DiT blocks over eight denoising steps, VAE, PNG —
21	and reproduces diffusers' fp32 CPU pipeline to **2.2e-2** of the decoded image.
22	Two runs agree to 14.18 s and 14.34 s. Every weight is resident: 7.17 GB of
23	text encoder, 12.54 GB of transformer, 0.30 GB of VAE and 4.90 GB of
24	activations, 21.9 s to load, and then images cost only their own time.
25	
26	Stage 9 took the last host arithmetic out of the denoising loop, the patch
27	embedder and the final layer: **59 ms of CPU a step to 5-10**. Stage 10 then
28	removed the two dispatches in the block that moved no information — `pack v`
29	and `narrow ctx`, each of them a tensor read back and written out in the shape
30	the next kernel wanted — by making them the *store instruction* of the kernel
31	above: **18 dispatches a block to 16**, 53.17 ms to **51.80**, an image 14.49 s
32	to **14.26**.
33	
34	So the whole of what is left is the DiT's arithmetic. The DiT is **94% of an
35	image**, and inside a block it is 74% GEMM at 73-76% of the WMMA ceiling, 14%
36	attention and 12% elementwise. Nothing outside it is worth a percent.
37	
38	**Target**: `prompt → PNG` for Z-Image-Turbo at 1024x1024, 8 steps, fp16.
39	
40	## Why this exists
41	
42	Phase 1 — fifteen-plus sessions of microbenchmarks — ended 2026-09-13 with no
43	convergence criterion (`TODO.md` carries the argument). **The unit of work is
44	now "a thing that runs", not "an experiment":** a profiler chooses the
45	optimisation targets, the backlog does not. Stage 4 is what that looks like —
46	it went looking for the kernel `results/shapes.csv` said would win, found it
47	the *slowest* in the ladder once the weight and the launch order were what the
48	memory system wanted, and closed three backlog items on the way without ever
49	having gone looking for them.
50	
51	## The model, as the checkpoint actually describes it
52	
53	Read with `go run ./cmd/inspect models/Z-Image-Turbo/<part>`. These differ
54	from `bench/modelshapes.go`, which was transcribed from `config.json` by
55	hand and has gaps that change the arithmetic:
56	
57	| | |
58	|---|---|
59	| DiT blocks | **34**, not 30 — 30 `layers` + 2 `context_refiner` + 2 `noise_refiner` |
60	| Width / heads | dim 3840, 30 heads, head_dim 128, `qk_norm` on `[128]` |
61	| Attention | four matrices `to_q`/`to_k`/`to_v`/`to_out.0`, each `[3840, 3840]`, **no biases** |
62	| FFN | SwiGLU: `w1`,`w3` `[10240, 3840]` gate/up, `w2` `[3840, 10240]` down |
63	| Modulation | `adaLN_modulation` `[15360, 256]` + bias per layer; chunks are scale_msa, gate_msa, scale_mlp, gate_mlp, the scales offset by one and the gates through tanh |
64	| RoPE | 3D, `axes_dims [32, 48, 48]`, `axes_lens [1536, 512, 512]`, theta 256 |
65	| Latents | 16 channels, patch size 2 — 1024x1024 is 128x128 latents is **4096 tokens** |
66	| VAE | Flux `AutoencoderKL`: `block_out_channels [128,256,512,512]`, 2 layers/block, GroupNorm(32), SiLU, mid-block attention, 8x upsample, scale 0.3611, shift 0.1159 |
67	| Text encoder | Qwen3-4B: 36 layers, hidden 2560, FFN 9728, GQA 32q/8kv, head_dim 128, vocab 151936 |
68	| Scheduler | `FlowMatchEulerDiscrete`, shift 3.0, 1000 train timesteps, 8 NFE |
69	| Topology | **three phases, three lengths**: noise refiners over the image tokens, context refiners over the caption, then the 30 layers over the two concatenated. The context refiners are `modulation=False` — no adaLN, no scale, ungated residuals |
70	
71	Sizes: transformer 6.155 B **F32** on disk (24.62 GB); text encoder 4.022 B
72	and VAE 0.084 B, both **BF16**. As fp16 the three total **20.5 GB**, so the
73	whole pipeline is resident in 128 GB unified memory at once.
74	
75	## Stages
76	
77	| # | Stage | State | Notes |
78	|---|---|---|---|
79	| 1 | Checkpoint loader | **done** | `safetensors/`, `cmd/inspect` |
80	| 2a | VAE decoder, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/vae/`, validated stagewise against diffusers |
81	| 2b | VAE decoder, Vulkan | **done** | 10 shaders, 119 dispatches, 1024² in 5.6 s |
82	| 3a | DiT block, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/dit/`, validated stagewise incl. RoPE and qk-norm |
83	| 3b | Attention, Vulkan, scalar | **done** | 4 shaders; 1.28 TFLOP/s, kept as the oracle |
84	| 3c | Attention on WMMA | **done** | 38.8 TFLOP/s = 70% of ceiling, 30.4x |
85	| 4a | The block as a graph | **done** | `GPUBlock`, 26 dispatches, 65.6 ms; §2.8 |
86	| 4b | Fuse the tail, fix `ff.w13` | **done** | 18 dispatches, **49.3 ms**; §2.4, §2.6 |
87	| 4c | 34 blocks | **done** | `GPUStack`, 3 weight banks, **1.60 s/step**, 12.8 s/image |
88	| 5a | Tokenizer | **done** | `zimage/tokenizer`, byte-level BPE, 20 cases id for id |
89	| 5b | Text encoder, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/qwen`, 35 of 36 layers, **2.08 s**; `cmd/textenc` |
90	| 5c | Text encoder, Vulkan | **done** | 21 dispatches/layer, 2 banks, **57 ms**; the winning tile moves with T |
91	| 6 | Scheduler + driver | **done** | `zimage/pipeline`, `cmd/zimage`; **19.8 s per image**, 2.5e-2 against diffusers |
92	| 7 | VAE mid block on WMMA | **done** | attention **94x**, projections **449x**; decode 5.65 s → **3.62 s**, image → **17.8 s**; §7 |
93	| 8 | conv2d on WMMA | **done** | implicit GEMM, **12.4x**; decode 3.62 s → **876 ms**, image → **15.0 s**; §8 |
94	| 9 | Head and tail on the device | **done** | host per step **59 ms → 5-10 ms**, image → **14.5 s**; §9 |
95	| 10 | The layout passes as epilogues | **done** | 18 dispatches → **16**, image → **14.26 s**; §10 |
96	
97	Each stage gets a CPU implementation in Go first: it separates "do I understand
98	the architecture" from "is the shader right", and once it matches diffusers it
99	is the oracle the GPU port is debugged against.
100	
101	## The rule for every stage
102	
103	Validate against the **library reference**, not against a shape table.
104	`reference/dump_vae.py` and `reference/dump_dit_block.py` are the pattern: run
105	a fixed input through diffusers in fp32 on CPU, dump **every submodule's
106	output**, and walk the graph stage by stage against it. Stage 5's oracle is
107	`transformers` rather than `diffusers` (`reference/dump_qwen.py`,
108	`reference/dump_tokenizer.py`) — same pattern, and it does one thing more:
109	where the port relies on an assumption about the library (which hidden state
110	`[-2]` is, whether padding changes an answer) the dump *measures* the
111	assumption and the test reads the number. `GPUBlock.RunTo` is
112	what makes that possible on an 18-dispatch graph whose intermediates are
113	overwritten before it ends: it re-runs the prefix up to a labelled dispatch.
114	
115	Five rules around that, each of which has caught something:
116	
117	- **A negative control per test**, deliberately breaking the implementation
118	  and asserting the break is caught. Without one the test proves only that it
119	  runs. `zimage/vae`'s land 141x-14000x above tolerance, stage 3c's 27x-569x,
120	  stage 4a's **1160x-15828x**.
121	- **When an optimisation removes a stage boundary, keep the slow path** and
122	  check the fast one against it at the last point its own output is visible.
123	  Stage 4b's fusions are bit-identical there; its fp16 store is not, and is
124	  measured separately for it rather than folded into one bound.
125	- **Normalise the error by the tensor's RMS**, not per element — but know what
126	  that costs: two of stage 4a's stages report 3e-2 where their worst element
127	  is 2e-3 of itself, because an RMS norm's output inherits the learned
128	  weight's dynamic range. Stage 5 is where that bill came due: Qwen3's
129	  massive activations put the absmax **109-238x** above the RMS, so the RMS
130	  alone fails a stage whose worst element is off by 9e-6 of itself. The
131	  denominator needs a floor — `max(|want|, rms)` per element — and **which
132	  denominator is right is a property of the model**, so look before
133	  inheriting one. Stage 6 needs a third answer: a denoising trajectory is
134	  chaotic, so it is bounded in **relative L2** over the whole tensor.
135	- **Validate the composition too, and do it at a small size.** Every stage's
136	  own oracle passed while the pipeline made a black image, because what was
137	  wrong was between them. `reference/dump_zimage_run.py` runs the whole
138	  diffusers pipeline in fp32 on the CPU at **256x256** — 3.2 s a step, the
139	  full eight steps and the VAE in half a minute — because the composition
140	  does not know how big the image is. It is the cheapest test in the project
141	  and it found three bugs in one sitting.
142	- **A real prompt is not a random tensor.** Two of stage 6's three bugs only
143	  appear on real inputs: SwiGLU's product overflows fp16 at 7.1e4 where the
144	  random fixture peaks at 5.1e4, and the VAE's watchdog cap only fails at the
145	  full image. Random-input validation is necessary and it is not sufficient.
146	
147	## What the kernels already give us
148	
149	Measured on this device (`research/`), and load-bearing for every stage:
150	
151	- **fp16 is the fast path.** WMMA fp16 is 55.5 TFLOP/s; WMMA int8 is the
152	  *same* rate, not double (§0). The DiT's projections reach **42.0, 76%**.
153	- **Do not quantize the DiT for speed.** At M=4096 its intensity is `4*M` =
154	  16384 flop/byte against a 235 crossover, so it is compute-bound and 4-bit
155	  weights buy nothing (§3.4). Quantize for footprint only.
156	- **Coverage law** (§5.1b): achievable bandwidth is
157	  `min(1, C/gcd(stride, 4096))`, C being the contiguous run the in-flight
158	  requests hold. Land `gcd` in [128, 256] B. Getting this wrong costs 2-8x.
159	- **Order, twice.** Store every WMMA operand as 16x16 fragment tiles (§2.8) —
160	  free on a weight, 1.43-1.46x — and walk the grid in bands of 8 columns
161	  rather than rows (§2.4), which keeps the resident workgroups a *block* of C
162	  instead of a row that streams all of B past one A slab: **1.84x** on the one
163	  shape wide enough to suffer, and only 1.16x without the tiling. They are one
164	  lever measured in two places.
165	- **Both halves of the roofline are in this pipeline, and they want opposite
166	  kernels.** The DiT is compute-bound at 16384 flop/byte; the text encoder

168	  against the same 235 crossover. Measured: the encoder's winning tile is 16
169	  or 32 rows at 24 tokens, 64 at 128, and the DiT's own 128x256 at 256+ —

171	  narrowest at a long one. Re-planning per run is free (`qwen.PlanFor`),

177	- **Time dispatches, not `Apply`** — but know which side of the heap you are
178	  on. A host read of the device-local host-visible arena runs at **0.18 GB/s**
179	  (writes: 29), so a wall-clock figure with a read-back in it is measuring the
180	  read-back. That heap's budget on this device is about **8 GB**, though, and
181	  `vk.NewBuffer` silently falls back to the plain host-visible one past it,
182	  where the same read runs at **15 GB/s** — so a single-stage benchmark and
183	  the 20.5 GB pipeline are on opposite sides of it and disagree by 83x on what
184	  a read-back costs. `cmd/bus` measures it; stage 9 found it.

186	## Measured baselines, per stage
187	
188	The stage-level figures the budget above is made of. Each stage's own
189	measurement harness is still there — `cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/vaebench`,
190	`cmd/textenc -gpu` — and each stage's research note has the sweep behind it.
191	
192	**The DiT** (`go run ./cmd/ditstack -image 4096 -caption 128`, GPU timestamps,
193	best of three, two runs agreeing to 51.78 and 51.82 ms a layer block):
194	
195	| phase | blocks | tokens | per block | total |
196	|---|---|---|---|---|
197	| `noise_refiner` | 2 | 4096 | 49.4 ms | 98.8 ms |
198	| `context_refiner` | 2 | 128 | 2.57 ms | 5.1 ms |
199	| `layers` | 30 | 4224 | **51.80 ms** | 1.55 s |
200	| **one step** | 34 | | | **1.66 s** |
201	
202	A block is 16 dispatches: **74% GEMM** (37.97 ms), 14% attention (7.19 ms) and
203	12% elementwise (5.93 ms across eight passes). One kernel
204	(`wg128x256_bt16_swz8`) wins all three of its shapes at **40.6-42.0 TFLOP/s**,
205	73-76% of the ceiling. Residency is 12.54 GB in three fp16 banks of 4.25, 4.25
206	and 3.54 GB holding 12, 12 and 10 blocks, plus a 0.51 GB fp32 arena and 1.29 GB
207	of activations, against an 83.79 GiB device-local host-visible heap.
208	
209	The layers phase measures 1.56 s of wall clock against 1.55 s of dispatches,
210	and in the pipeline a step is 1.67-1.70 s against the same 1.66 — 10 ms of
211	host and 9 of bus, and the ~50 ms remainder is the one thing in this budget

214	**The VAE** (`go run ./cmd/vaebench`), every convolution and the mid block on

216	
217	| latent | image | fp32 arena | fp16 arena | wall | before stage 8 |
218	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
219	| 16² | 128² | 46 MB | 9 MB | 13 ms | 47 ms |
220	| 32² | 256² | 185 MB | 34 MB | 46 ms | 192 ms |
221	| 64² | 512² | 738 MB | 135 MB | 204 ms | 856 ms |

243	## Where the image budget stands
244	
245	`go run ./cmd/zimage -width 1024`, wall clock, two runs agreeing to 14.18 s
246	and 14.34 s.

248	| | per image, 1024², 8 steps | share |
249	|---|---|---|
250	| denoising | **13.37 s** | 93.8% |

259	transformer, 0.30 GB of VAE weights, 4.90 GB of activation arenas.

262	text encoder, caption refiners, VAE, and now the head and tail — is 6.4%

295	## What each stage found
296	
297	One file per stage in `research/`, indexed in `research/README.md`. The ones
298	that are load-bearing for what is left:
299	
300	- **[Stage 10, the layout epilogues](research/stage-10-layout-epilogues.md)**
301	  — the two dispatches in the block that moved no information, absorbed into
302	  the store of the kernel above: **18 a block to 16**, an image 14.49 s to
303	  14.26. Possible at all because in both cases the data was already in the
304	  right registers in the right 16x16 shape, so a transposed fragment tile is
305	  a *column-major `coopMatStore` of stride 16* and not a transpose. Two other
306	  things fell out: the item had been mispriced 3.4x by a units slip
307	  (`1.0 ms a block` quoted as `1.0 s an image`), and the old path was doing a
308	  **double rounding** — which is why 84 halves in 1.2 M of the context differ
309	  and why every one of them is an exact fp16 tie.
310	- **[Stage 2, the VAE](research/stage-2-vae-decoder.md)** — two hard device
311	  limits that still bind: 4.29 GB per storage buffer, and a reset watchdog
312	  that kills a multi-second command buffer. Its absmax survey (497 through the
313	  decoder, 1.16e7 in the mid block's scores) is what stages 7 and 8 narrowed
314	  against, and is now asserted by `TestConvInputsFitFP16`.
315	- **[Stage 3, attention](research/stage-3-dit-attention.md)** — 70% of the WMMA
316	  ceiling, but only once every operand is stored as fragment tiles. Three port
317	  hazards: RoPE pairs *adjacent* components, the q/k norms are *per head*, and

319	- **[Stage 4, the block](research/stage-4-dit-graph.md)** — 90.0 ms/block to
320	  **49.3**, none of it arithmetic. The interactions are the finding: the
321	  swizzle is worth 1.84x on a tiled weight and 1.16x on a row-major one, the
322	  hoisted K-slab becomes a *loss* on a tiled weight, and once all of it is
323	  applied the three shapes that disagreed on a kernel stop disagreeing.
324	- **[Stage 5, the text encoder](research/stage-5-text-encoder.md)** — **2.08 s
325	  to 57 ms**, and the encoder sits on the **memory-bound** half of the
326	  roofline, so unlike the DiT its winning kernel *moves with the prompt
327	  length* and re-planning per run is free. Three conventions invert between it
328	  and the DiT — NeoX RoPE, causal attention, grouped heads — and Qwen3's
329	  massive activations break an RMS-normalised error bound.
330	- **[Stage 6, the pipeline](research/stage-6-pipeline.md)** — every bug this
331	  stage had was in the *composition* and invisible to each component's own
332	  oracle: SwiGLU's product **overflows fp16 on a real prompt and never on a
333	  random one**, a new push constant on a shared shader silently zeroed the
334	  text encoder's feed-forward, and a dispatches-per-submit cap is a proxy for
335	  a time cap that stops being one when the dispatches differ 100x. Also: the
336	  context refiners take neither the timestep nor the latents, so **two of the
337	  three phases run once per image rather than once per step**.
338	- **[Stage 7, the VAE mid block](research/stage-7-vae-mid-block.md)** —
339	  attention **1.43 s → 15.1 ms**, the four projections **503 ms → 1.12 ms**.
340	  The finding that outlives the stage: this block's softmax is so saturated
341	  that a kernel **dropping three quarters of every dot product decodes the
342	  same image**, so no end-to-end tolerance can validate it.
343	- **[Stage 9, the head and tail](research/stage-9-head-and-tail.md)** — the
344	  host's share of a step **59 ms → 5-10 ms**. A bias and a *pad token* become
345	  extra columns of K, so `y = Wx + b` and `y = x_pad_token` come out of one
346	  biasless GEMM. And the correction that matters beyond this stage: the
347	  engine's "a host read-back runs at 0.2 GB/s" holds only below **~8 GB of
348	  allocation**, where `vk.NewBuffer` still gets the device-local heap; the
349	  20.5 GB pipeline reads the same arena **83x faster**, which is why the 0.8 s
350	  an image this stage was partly priced on was never there (`cmd/bus`).
351	- **[Stage 8, conv2d](research/stage-8-vae-conv.md)** — the last operator in
352	  the VAE, **3.02 s → 244 ms** at 41-42 TFLOP/s. The finding is the layout: a
353	  patch fragment is contiguous only if the **channel** axis is the tiled one,
354	  because tiling the pixel axis — what every other operand in this engine does
355	  — makes the `dw = ±1` window straddle two tiles. Also: §2.7's K-slab hoist
356	  does **nothing** once both operands are fully covered.
357	- **[Stage 4c, the stack](research/stage-4c-dit-stack.md)** — splitting a
358	  12.0 GB weight arena across storage buffers costs **one pipeline per bank
359	  and nothing per dispatch**; six banks are bit-identical to one.

# PIPELINE — the z-image-turbo vertical slice

> **PARKED 2026-09-14, and this file is the record of where.** The current
> work is [`SPEECH.md`](SPEECH.md) — the parakeet and kokoro verticals — and
> this slice resumes after them. Nothing below is stale: it is the state the
> pipeline is in, and the three items under "Where the image budget stands"
> are where to pick it up. The short version: an image is **14.26 s**, the DiT
> is **94%** of it, and the only thing left worth more than a percent is the
> **quarter of the WMMA ceiling the seven projections do not reach — 2.6 s**.

> **This file is rewritten, not appended.** It states where the pipeline is
> *now* and what happens next. History belongs in `TODO.md` (session
> handoffs) and `research/` (closed findings); if a paragraph here is about
> the past, it is in the wrong file. Keep it under ~200 lines — it earns a
> few more with each stage that closes, and loses them when a stage's detail
> moves to `research/`.

**Status**: **the target is met, and the block has no layout work left in it.**
`go run ./cmd/zimage -prompt "..."` writes a 1024x1024 PNG in **14.3 s** —
tokenizer, text encoder, 34 DiT blocks over eight denoising steps, VAE, PNG —
and reproduces diffusers' fp32 CPU pipeline to **2.2e-2** of the decoded image.
Two runs agree to 14.18 s and 14.34 s. Every weight is resident: 7.17 GB of
text encoder, 12.54 GB of transformer, 0.30 GB of VAE and 4.90 GB of
activations, 21.9 s to load, and then images cost only their own time.

Stage 9 took the last host arithmetic out of the denoising loop, the patch
embedder and the final layer: **59 ms of CPU a step to 5-10**. Stage 10 then
removed the two dispatches in the block that moved no information — `pack v`
and `narrow ctx`, each of them a tensor read back and written out in the shape
the next kernel wanted — by making them the *store instruction* of the kernel
above: **18 dispatches a block to 16**, 53.17 ms to **51.80**, an image 14.49 s
to **14.26**.

So the whole of what is left is the DiT's arithmetic. The DiT is **94% of an
image**, and inside a block it is 74% GEMM at 73-76% of the WMMA ceiling, 14%
attention and 12% elementwise. Nothing outside it is worth a percent.

**Target**: `prompt → PNG` for Z-Image-Turbo at 1024x1024, 8 steps, fp16.

## Why this exists

Phase 1 — fifteen-plus sessions of microbenchmarks — ended 2026-09-13 with no
convergence criterion (`TODO.md` carries the argument). **The unit of work is
now "a thing that runs", not "an experiment":** a profiler chooses the
optimisation targets, the backlog does not. Stage 4 is what that looks like —
it went looking for the kernel `results/shapes.csv` said would win, found it
the *slowest* in the ladder once the weight and the launch order were what the
memory system wanted, and closed three backlog items on the way without ever
having gone looking for them.

## The model, as the checkpoint actually describes it

Read with `go run ./cmd/inspect models/Z-Image-Turbo/<part>`. These differ
from `bench/modelshapes.go`, which was transcribed from `config.json` by
hand and has gaps that change the arithmetic:

| | |
|---|---|
| DiT blocks | **34**, not 30 — 30 `layers` + 2 `context_refiner` + 2 `noise_refiner` |
| Width / heads | dim 3840, 30 heads, head_dim 128, `qk_norm` on `[128]` |
| Attention | four matrices `to_q`/`to_k`/`to_v`/`to_out.0`, each `[3840, 3840]`, **no biases** |
| FFN | SwiGLU: `w1`,`w3` `[10240, 3840]` gate/up, `w2` `[3840, 10240]` down |
| Modulation | `adaLN_modulation` `[15360, 256]` + bias per layer; chunks are scale_msa, gate_msa, scale_mlp, gate_mlp, the scales offset by one and the gates through tanh |
| RoPE | 3D, `axes_dims [32, 48, 48]`, `axes_lens [1536, 512, 512]`, theta 256 |
| Latents | 16 channels, patch size 2 — 1024x1024 is 128x128 latents is **4096 tokens** |
| VAE | Flux `AutoencoderKL`: `block_out_channels [128,256,512,512]`, 2 layers/block, GroupNorm(32), SiLU, mid-block attention, 8x upsample, scale 0.3611, shift 0.1159 |
| Text encoder | Qwen3-4B: 36 layers, hidden 2560, FFN 9728, GQA 32q/8kv, head_dim 128, vocab 151936 |
| Scheduler | `FlowMatchEulerDiscrete`, shift 3.0, 1000 train timesteps, 8 NFE |
| Topology | **three phases, three lengths**: noise refiners over the image tokens, context refiners over the caption, then the 30 layers over the two concatenated. The context refiners are `modulation=False` — no adaLN, no scale, ungated residuals |

Sizes: transformer 6.155 B **F32** on disk (24.62 GB); text encoder 4.022 B
and VAE 0.084 B, both **BF16**. As fp16 the three total **20.5 GB**, so the
whole pipeline is resident in 128 GB unified memory at once.

## Stages

| # | Stage | State | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Checkpoint loader | **done** | `safetensors/`, `cmd/inspect` |
| 2a | VAE decoder, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/vae/`, validated stagewise against diffusers |
| 2b | VAE decoder, Vulkan | **done** | 10 shaders, 119 dispatches, 1024² in 5.6 s |
| 3a | DiT block, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/dit/`, validated stagewise incl. RoPE and qk-norm |
| 3b | Attention, Vulkan, scalar | **done** | 4 shaders; 1.28 TFLOP/s, kept as the oracle |
| 3c | Attention on WMMA | **done** | 38.8 TFLOP/s = 70% of ceiling, 30.4x |
| 4a | The block as a graph | **done** | `GPUBlock`, 26 dispatches, 65.6 ms; §2.8 |
| 4b | Fuse the tail, fix `ff.w13` | **done** | 18 dispatches, **49.3 ms**; §2.4, §2.6 |
| 4c | 34 blocks | **done** | `GPUStack`, 3 weight banks, **1.60 s/step**, 12.8 s/image |
| 5a | Tokenizer | **done** | `zimage/tokenizer`, byte-level BPE, 20 cases id for id |
| 5b | Text encoder, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/qwen`, 35 of 36 layers, **2.08 s**; `cmd/textenc` |
| 5c | Text encoder, Vulkan | **done** | 21 dispatches/layer, 2 banks, **57 ms**; the winning tile moves with T |
| 6 | Scheduler + driver | **done** | `zimage/pipeline`, `cmd/zimage`; **19.8 s per image**, 2.5e-2 against diffusers |
| 7 | VAE mid block on WMMA | **done** | attention **94x**, projections **449x**; decode 5.65 s → **3.62 s**, image → **17.8 s**; §7 |
| 8 | conv2d on WMMA | **done** | implicit GEMM, **12.4x**; decode 3.62 s → **876 ms**, image → **15.0 s**; §8 |
| 9 | Head and tail on the device | **done** | host per step **59 ms → 5-10 ms**, image → **14.5 s**; §9 |
| 10 | The layout passes as epilogues | **done** | 18 dispatches → **16**, image → **14.26 s**; §10 |

Each stage gets a CPU implementation in Go first: it separates "do I understand
the architecture" from "is the shader right", and once it matches diffusers it
is the oracle the GPU port is debugged against.

## The rule for every stage

Validate against the **library reference**, not against a shape table.
`reference/dump_vae.py` and `reference/dump_dit_block.py` are the pattern: run
a fixed input through diffusers in fp32 on CPU, dump **every submodule's
output**, and walk the graph stage by stage against it. Stage 5's oracle is
`transformers` rather than `diffusers` (`reference/dump_qwen.py`,
`reference/dump_tokenizer.py`) — same pattern, and it does one thing more:
where the port relies on an assumption about the library (which hidden state
`[-2]` is, whether padding changes an answer) the dump *measures* the
assumption and the test reads the number. `GPUBlock.RunTo` is
what makes that possible on an 18-dispatch graph whose intermediates are
overwritten before it ends: it re-runs the prefix up to a labelled dispatch.

Five rules around that, each of which has caught something:

- **A negative control per test**, deliberately breaking the implementation
  and asserting the break is caught. Without one the test proves only that it
  runs. `zimage/vae`'s land 141x-14000x above tolerance, stage 3c's 27x-569x,
  stage 4a's **1160x-15828x**.
- **When an optimisation removes a stage boundary, keep the slow path** and
  check the fast one against it at the last point its own output is visible.
  Stage 4b's fusions are bit-identical there; its fp16 store is not, and is
  measured separately for it rather than folded into one bound.
- **Normalise the error by the tensor's RMS**, not per element — but know what
  that costs: two of stage 4a's stages report 3e-2 where their worst element
  is 2e-3 of itself, because an RMS norm's output inherits the learned
  weight's dynamic range. Stage 5 is where that bill came due: Qwen3's
  massive activations put the absmax **109-238x** above the RMS, so the RMS
  alone fails a stage whose worst element is off by 9e-6 of itself. The
  denominator needs a floor — `max(|want|, rms)` per element — and **which
  denominator is right is a property of the model**, so look before
  inheriting one. Stage 6 needs a third answer: a denoising trajectory is
  chaotic, so it is bounded in **relative L2** over the whole tensor.
- **Validate the composition too, and do it at a small size.** Every stage's
  own oracle passed while the pipeline made a black image, because what was
  wrong was between them. `reference/dump_zimage_run.py` runs the whole
  diffusers pipeline in fp32 on the CPU at **256x256** — 3.2 s a step, the
  full eight steps and the VAE in half a minute — because the composition
  does not know how big the image is. It is the cheapest test in the project
  and it found three bugs in one sitting.
- **A real prompt is not a random tensor.** Two of stage 6's three bugs only
  appear on real inputs: SwiGLU's product overflows fp16 at 7.1e4 where the
  random fixture peaks at 5.1e4, and the VAE's watchdog cap only fails at the
  full image. Random-input validation is necessary and it is not sufficient.

## What the kernels already give us

Measured on this device (`research/`), and load-bearing for every stage:

- **fp16 is the fast path.** WMMA fp16 is 55.5 TFLOP/s; WMMA int8 is the
  *same* rate, not double (§0). The DiT's projections reach **42.0, 76%**.
- **Do not quantize the DiT for speed.** At M=4096 its intensity is `4*M` =
  16384 flop/byte against a 235 crossover, so it is compute-bound and 4-bit
  weights buy nothing (§3.4). Quantize for footprint only.
- **Coverage law** (§5.1b): achievable bandwidth is
  `min(1, C/gcd(stride, 4096))`, C being the contiguous run the in-flight
  requests hold. Land `gcd` in [128, 256] B. Getting this wrong costs 2-8x.
- **Order, twice.** Store every WMMA operand as 16x16 fragment tiles (§2.8) —
  free on a weight, 1.43-1.46x — and walk the grid in bands of 8 columns
  rather than rows (§2.4), which keeps the resident workgroups a *block* of C
  instead of a row that streams all of B past one A slab: **1.84x** on the one
  shape wide enough to suffer, and only 1.16x without the tiling. They are one
  lever measured in two places.
- **Both halves of the roofline are in this pipeline, and they want opposite
  kernels.** The DiT is compute-bound at 16384 flop/byte; the text encoder
  runs the same kind of layer at `T` flop/byte, which for a prompt is 8-512
  against the same 235 crossover. Measured: the encoder's winning tile is 16
  or 32 rows at 24 tokens, 64 at 128, and the DiT's own 128x256 at 256+ —
  1.24x for taking the DiT's default at a short prompt, 1.92x for taking the
  narrowest at a long one. Re-planning per run is free (`qwen.PlanFor`),
  because every rung reads the same staged weight.
- **Kernel choice is per shape only while something else is wrong.** The DiT's
  three shapes disagreed until both of the above were applied; then one kernel
  won all three. `results/shapes.csv`'s pick measures 23.5 s/image against
  13.4.
- **Time dispatches, not `Apply`** — but know which side of the heap you are
  on. A host read of the device-local host-visible arena runs at **0.18 GB/s**
  (writes: 29), so a wall-clock figure with a read-back in it is measuring the
  read-back. That heap's budget on this device is about **8 GB**, though, and
  `vk.NewBuffer` silently falls back to the plain host-visible one past it,
  where the same read runs at **15 GB/s** — so a single-stage benchmark and
  the 20.5 GB pipeline are on opposite sides of it and disagree by 83x on what
  a read-back costs. `cmd/bus` measures it; stage 9 found it.

## Measured baselines, per stage

The stage-level figures the budget above is made of. Each stage's own
measurement harness is still there — `cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/vaebench`,
`cmd/textenc -gpu` — and each stage's research note has the sweep behind it.

**The DiT** (`go run ./cmd/ditstack -image 4096 -caption 128`, GPU timestamps,
best of three, two runs agreeing to 51.78 and 51.82 ms a layer block):

| phase | blocks | tokens | per block | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `noise_refiner` | 2 | 4096 | 49.4 ms | 98.8 ms |
| `context_refiner` | 2 | 128 | 2.57 ms | 5.1 ms |
| `layers` | 30 | 4224 | **51.80 ms** | 1.55 s |
| **one step** | 34 | | | **1.66 s** |

A block is 16 dispatches: **74% GEMM** (37.97 ms), 14% attention (7.19 ms) and
12% elementwise (5.93 ms across eight passes). One kernel
(`wg128x256_bt16_swz8`) wins all three of its shapes at **40.6-42.0 TFLOP/s**,
73-76% of the ceiling. Residency is 12.54 GB in three fp16 banks of 4.25, 4.25
and 3.54 GB holding 12, 12 and 10 blocks, plus a 0.51 GB fp32 arena and 1.29 GB
of activations, against an 83.79 GiB device-local host-visible heap.

The layers phase measures 1.56 s of wall clock against 1.55 s of dispatches,
and in the pipeline a step is 1.67-1.70 s against the same 1.66 — 10 ms of
host and 9 of bus, and the ~50 ms remainder is the one thing in this budget
still unaccounted for (stage 9 ruled out submit batching for it).

**The VAE** (`go run ./cmd/vaebench`), every convolution and the mid block on
the matrix cores, wall clock including a read-back:

| latent | image | fp32 arena | fp16 arena | wall | before stage 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16² | 128² | 46 MB | 9 MB | 13 ms | 47 ms |
| 32² | 256² | 185 MB | 34 MB | 46 ms | 192 ms |
| 64² | 512² | 738 MB | 135 MB | 204 ms | 856 ms |
| 128² | **1024²** | 2.95 GB | 539 MB | **876 ms** | 3.62 s |

The wall column includes a read-back that the *pipeline* does not pay — 12.58
MB at the 0.18 GB/s a 3.5 GB program gets, 71 ms — which is why a decode costs
805 ms inside an image and 876 on its own (stage 9).

There is **no arithmetic left in this decoder**: conv3x3 is 244 ms at 41-42
TFLOP/s (30%) and the next four items are bandwidth-bound elementwise passes
running back to back over the same tensors — group norm 244 ms, the conv pack
160, SiLU 61, the adds 40, **63% together**. So what it wants next is not a
kernel but **fusion**, the same shape of change as stage 10: a SiLU whose only
consumer is a convolution could write the blocked fp16 form *instead of* its
fp32 output. ~200 ms of 805, and 1.4% of an image.

**The text encoder** (`go run ./cmd/textenc -gpu`), 35 layers, 7.07 GB of fp16
weights in two banks: **57.1 ms** at 24 tokens, 71.4 at 128, 170 at 512,
against 2.08 s and 9.17 s on the CPU. One run walks the roofline — the weights
are read once whatever T is, so GB/s of weight falling (124, 99, 42) *is*
GFLOP/s rising (3.0, 12.7, 21.2 T). 0.4% of an image; detail in
[`research/stage-5-text-encoder.md`](research/stage-5-text-encoder.md).

## Where the image budget stands

`go run ./cmd/zimage -width 1024`, wall clock, two runs agreeing to 14.18 s
and 14.34 s.

| | per image, 1024², 8 steps | share |
|---|---|---|
| denoising | **13.37 s** | 93.8% |
| — of which the 34 blocks | 13.3 s | 93.1% |
| — of which the host | 0.08 s | 0.6% |
| VAE decode | **0.81 s** | 5.7% |
| text encoder, 19 tokens | 0.06 s | 0.4% |
| caption refiners, once per image | 0.006 s | 0.04% |
| **total** | **14.26 s** | |

Loading is 21.9 s and happens once: 7.17 GB of text encoder, 12.54 GB of
transformer, 0.30 GB of VAE weights, 4.90 GB of activation arenas.

**The image is the DiT and nothing else.** Everything outside it — tokenizer,
text encoder, caption refiners, VAE, and now the head and tail — is 6.4%
together, and no item in it is worth more than 1.3%. There is no boundary work
left: the host does a patchify and an unpatchify on a megabyte, and the bus
carries 1 MB each way per step.

And inside the block there is no *layout* left either — stage 10 took the last
of it. Everything remaining is arithmetic or the traffic arithmetic needs:

- **The seven projections, 9.9 s an image (69%), at 73-76% of the WMMA
  ceiling.** The quarter they do not reach is 2.6 s, which is an order of
  magnitude more than everything else in this list together. It is also the
  hardest: stage 4 already applied the fragment-tiled weight (§2.8), the
  banded grid (§2.4) and the hoisted K-slab (§2.7), and the ablation behind
  `results/gemm_wmma.csv` is 1.25x behind what the pipeline already does.
- **Attention at 38 TFLOP/s**, 1.9 s an image, against the GEMMs' 40.6-42.0.
  Worth ~0.2 s if it caught up. Stage 10 halved its store and removed its LDS
  staging and neither moved it, which agrees with stage 3c that the register
  file is what binds it.
- **The eight elementwise passes, 5.93 ms a block and 1.6 s an image.** Each
  reads the residual stream and writes it; `swiglu` (1.45 ms) and the two
  gated residuals (0.89, 0.85) are half. Unlike stage 10's two they compute
  something, so what they want is fusion into a neighbour — and the neighbour
  is usually a GEMM, which is where §2.6 and stage 10 both ended.

Below those: the VAE's elementwise fusions are ~200 ms (1.4%) and the text
encoder's remaining 1.9x is worth less than a percent.

**One correction worth carrying**, because it sat at the top of this list for
four sessions: the layout item was priced here at "~1.0 s an image" and was
**~0.29 s**. The measurement it came from (stage 4) said 1.0 **ms a block**
and the unit was lost in transcription. A number quoted between documents
should carry the dimension it was measured in.

## What each stage found

One file per stage in `research/`, indexed in `research/README.md`. The ones
that are load-bearing for what is left:

- **[Stage 10, the layout epilogues](research/stage-10-layout-epilogues.md)**
  — the two dispatches in the block that moved no information, absorbed into
  the store of the kernel above: **18 a block to 16**, an image 14.49 s to
  14.26. Possible at all because in both cases the data was already in the
  right registers in the right 16x16 shape, so a transposed fragment tile is
  a *column-major `coopMatStore` of stride 16* and not a transpose. Two other
  things fell out: the item had been mispriced 3.4x by a units slip
  (`1.0 ms a block` quoted as `1.0 s an image`), and the old path was doing a
  **double rounding** — which is why 84 halves in 1.2 M of the context differ
  and why every one of them is an exact fp16 tie.
- **[Stage 2, the VAE](research/stage-2-vae-decoder.md)** — two hard device
  limits that still bind: 4.29 GB per storage buffer, and a reset watchdog
  that kills a multi-second command buffer. Its absmax survey (497 through the
  decoder, 1.16e7 in the mid block's scores) is what stages 7 and 8 narrowed
  against, and is now asserted by `TestConvInputsFitFP16`.
- **[Stage 3, attention](research/stage-3-dit-attention.md)** — 70% of the WMMA
  ceiling, but only once every operand is stored as fragment tiles. Three port
  hazards: RoPE pairs *adjacent* components, the q/k norms are *per head*, and
  v is the operand that needs transposing.
- **[Stage 4, the block](research/stage-4-dit-graph.md)** — 90.0 ms/block to
  **49.3**, none of it arithmetic. The interactions are the finding: the
  swizzle is worth 1.84x on a tiled weight and 1.16x on a row-major one, the
  hoisted K-slab becomes a *loss* on a tiled weight, and once all of it is
  applied the three shapes that disagreed on a kernel stop disagreeing.
- **[Stage 5, the text encoder](research/stage-5-text-encoder.md)** — **2.08 s
  to 57 ms**, and the encoder sits on the **memory-bound** half of the
  roofline, so unlike the DiT its winning kernel *moves with the prompt
  length* and re-planning per run is free. Three conventions invert between it
  and the DiT — NeoX RoPE, causal attention, grouped heads — and Qwen3's
  massive activations break an RMS-normalised error bound.
- **[Stage 6, the pipeline](research/stage-6-pipeline.md)** — every bug this
  stage had was in the *composition* and invisible to each component's own
  oracle: SwiGLU's product **overflows fp16 on a real prompt and never on a
  random one**, a new push constant on a shared shader silently zeroed the
  text encoder's feed-forward, and a dispatches-per-submit cap is a proxy for
  a time cap that stops being one when the dispatches differ 100x. Also: the
  context refiners take neither the timestep nor the latents, so **two of the
  three phases run once per image rather than once per step**.
- **[Stage 7, the VAE mid block](research/stage-7-vae-mid-block.md)** —
  attention **1.43 s → 15.1 ms**, the four projections **503 ms → 1.12 ms**.
  The finding that outlives the stage: this block's softmax is so saturated
  that a kernel **dropping three quarters of every dot product decodes the
  same image**, so no end-to-end tolerance can validate it.
- **[Stage 9, the head and tail](research/stage-9-head-and-tail.md)** — the
  host's share of a step **59 ms → 5-10 ms**. A bias and a *pad token* become
  extra columns of K, so `y = Wx + b` and `y = x_pad_token` come out of one
  biasless GEMM. And the correction that matters beyond this stage: the
  engine's "a host read-back runs at 0.2 GB/s" holds only below **~8 GB of
  allocation**, where `vk.NewBuffer` still gets the device-local heap; the
  20.5 GB pipeline reads the same arena **83x faster**, which is why the 0.8 s
  an image this stage was partly priced on was never there (`cmd/bus`).
- **[Stage 8, conv2d](research/stage-8-vae-conv.md)** — the last operator in
  the VAE, **3.02 s → 244 ms** at 41-42 TFLOP/s. The finding is the layout: a
  patch fragment is contiguous only if the **channel** axis is the tiled one,
  because tiling the pixel axis — what every other operand in this engine does
  — makes the `dw = ±1` window straddle two tiles. Also: §2.7's K-slab hoist
  does **nothing** once both operands are fully covered.
- **[Stage 4c, the stack](research/stage-4c-dit-stack.md)** — splitting a
  12.0 GB weight arena across storage buffers costs **one pipeline per bank
  and nothing per dispatch**; six banks are bit-identical to one.

88	concede nothing the reference keeps. **L2f then put that layer on the device**:
89	six dispatches where the reference has nineteen, **66.3 ms of its 512-token

91	at equal work** — by fusing six of its matrices into one `[13952, 2560]`
92	projection, the two norms, the two ropes and the fragment tiling into one pass,
93	and the output gate into the attention epilogue. It also found the same kernel
94	wanting **opposite BM schedules on two weights that differ only in falling
95	either side of the 32 MiB MALL**. Two of the three dense blocks are now on the
96	device, and between them they take **25.1% of llama.cpp's prefill graph down to
97	7.0%**. The Go
98	side reads the
99	checkpoint: `gguf/` (1224/1224 tensors against the Python inventory), five
100	dequant paths bit-exact against ggml, and a tokenizer exact against
101	`llama-tokenize`. The plan behind it is unchanged — run the stock quant first
102	(llama.cpp is the oracle), then re-quantise, because **76% of the bytes read
103	per token are dense** and the stock Q8_0 dense allocation costs 1.7x on a
104	bus-bound machine. Task list L0–L9. **L3, L4 and L5 have since closed — every block of the model
105	has a kernel — L6a put all 48 layers of all five of them on the device at
106	once, L6b closed the loop (the model runs end to end and the last token's
107	argmax is llama.cpp's own out of llama.cpp's own top ten), and L6c took the
108	glue between blocks off the host. Prefill is 941.3 tok/s at ubatch 2048
109	against the reference's 391.42 — 2.40x — with 96.6% of the pass inside the
110	five blocks. What is left of prefill is inside the kernels, not between them;
111	the next stage is L7, decode.** **L7 then closed the loop** — a prompt in,
112	tokens out, over a cache the last step extends, writing llama.cpp's own
113	completion at temperature zero — and **phase 2 is most of the way through its
114	bank half**: L8a and L8b put every dense weight on the width the checkpoint
115	already ships, L8d and L8e gave every block that dominates a decode step a
116	kernel shaped for one row, and L8c-4 through L8c-7 put the lm head, the 36
117	gated DeltaNet layers, the 97 hyper-connection mixers and the 12
118	full-attention layers with their QSA indexers on **4.5 bits**. **Decode is
119	31.5 tok/s against llama.cpp's 25.15 — 1.25x — prefill 1071.8 at ubatch 2048
120	against 391.42, residency 79.85 GB, and perplexity 4.1787 against our own
121	4.0289 at identical weights, +3.72%.** One dense family is left (`ple_proj`),
122	and the sharpest open item is not a width: **the whole-model graph never
123	returns above ~2560 rows at 48 layers.** All three files are rewritten each
124	session rather than appended to, and the current one is the file to read
125	first.
126	
127	Three documents carry the older analysis: **`IDEAS.md`** is the prioritised
128	experiment backlog (~30 items, each with hypothesis / change / expected
129	gain / how to measure, and marked up with what has since been measured),
130	plus the measured roofline and the order of attack. **`research/`** is the
131	findings archive — one file per *completed* section, indexed in
132	`research/README.md`; when an item closes, its write-up moves there and
133	`IDEAS.md` keeps the heading, a one-line result and a link. **`GOALS.md`**
134	is the long-term target (five models, HTTP API in Go).
135	
136	`§N.M` is the stable address across all of them and is cited from the code
137	itself (293 comments in `shaders/`, `bench/`, `cmd/`, `vk/`). Never
138	renumber a section; give a new experiment the next free number.
139	
140	## Phase 2 — build the pipeline, profile it, then optimise
141	
142	The microbenchmark phase ended 2026-09-13. The current plan, the model's
143	real dimensions and the stage list live in **[`PIPELINE.md`](PIPELINE.md)**,
144	which is *rewritten* each session rather than appended to. Session handoffs
145	still accumulate below.
146	
147	**Session 2026-09-13 (the pivot):** `safetensors/` (mmap checkpoint reader, F32/F16/BF16,
148	sharded and single-file) and `cmd/inspect`. Verified against 10,574 golden
149	narrowing cases from CPython's `struct 'e'`, an exhaustive 65,536-pattern
150	fp16 round trip, and a value-for-value cross-check of real tensors against
151	an independent Python read. The golden table caught a real bug: the
152	underflow boundary was one exponent too high, so values in [2^-25, 2^-24)
153	flushed to zero instead of rounding up to the smallest subnormal.
154	
155	This is the first time the project has loaded a real checkpoint, and it
156	immediately corrected the hand-transcribed shape table — the DiT has **34
157	attention blocks, not 30**, and `adaLN_modulation` was not modelled at all.
158	See `PIPELINE.md` for the full inventory.

1	# API — the models behind one HTTP server
2	
3	`cmd/serve` is the long-lived process: an OpenAI-shaped API over the models in
4	this repository, with one flag per vertical deciding what is resident.
5	
6	    go run ./cmd/serve -llm -embed -tts -stt
7	
8	`GOALS.md`'s last line — "we will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these
9	features, in Go" — is what this is. It is stage one of that: the routing
10	layer, four of the five verticals wired to it, and the shape the fifth plugs
11	into.
12	
13	## What answers today
14	
15	| Endpoint | State |
16	|---|---|
17	| `GET /v1/models` | **done** — lists what the process actually loaded, with the speech model's voices |
18	| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | **done** — qwen3.8-flash-next, `-llm`, buffered and SSE |
19	| `POST /v1/responses` | **done** — the same generation, OpenAI's newer envelope |
20	| `POST /v1/messages` | **done** — the same generation, Anthropic's envelope |
21	| `POST /v1/audio/speech` | **done** — kokoro, `-tts` |
22	| `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` | **done** — parakeet, `-stt`, with word and segment timings |
23	| `POST /v1/embeddings` | **done** — Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, `-embed`, float or base64, MRL widths |
24	| `POST /v1/images/generations`, `/edits` | 501 — `zimage/pipeline` runs, it is not wired here |
25	
26	Every endpoint is *routed*, including the ones that are not implemented: a
27	client gets a 501 that says what is missing and, where a flag would have fixed
28	it, which flag. A 404 would mean a misspelled path and nothing else.
29	
30	## The three packages
31	
32	    cmd/serve   flags, load order, graceful shutdown
33	    backend/    the adapters: weights, device residency, one lock each
34	    api/        routing, request shapes, encoding; imports no model
35	
36	The direction of the dependency is `cmd/serve -> backend -> api`, never the
37	other way. `api` *declares* the backend interfaces (`api.SpeechBackend`,
38	`api.TranscriptionBackend`, `api.CompletionBackend`, `api.EmbeddingBackend`)
39	and implements none of them, so it pulls in no checkpoint loader and no Vulkan, and its tests run
40	against fakes in milliseconds — `go test ./api/` needs no `models/` directory
41	and no GPU, including for the three chat envelopes and their streams.
42	
43	What crosses the boundary is deliberately model-shaped and not
44	container-shaped. A speech backend returns `*audio.Clip` — samples and a rate
45	— and the HTTP layer encodes the WAV or the raw PCM, because which one was
46	asked for is the request's business and not the model's. A transcription
47	backend is handed an already-decoded clip for the same reason in reverse.
48	
49	**The completion backend's signature is a streaming one**, and the buffered
50	response is written in terms of it rather than the other way round. A token
51	on this part costs ~44 ms of the wall clock at 22.7 tok/s, so a 500-token
52	answer is 22 seconds: an interface that returned the whole thing would make
53	the streamed endpoint impossible to build on top of it, where the buffered one
54	is a string builder over the streaming one. That is also what keeps the two
55	answers to the same prompt identical — a server whose streaming path is a
56	separate implementation is a server whose two answers eventually differ, over
57	some whitespace one of them strips.
58	
59	## The log does not keep the conversations
60	
61	`-log-bodies` is off by default, and that default is the point: this server's
62	request and response bodies are its users' prompts and answers, and a process
63	that stays up would otherwise write every one of them to disk as a side effect
64	of having an access log. With it off the log still carries the method, the
65	path, the status, the duration and the sizes — which is what an operator reads
66	anyway. An event stream is never kept whatever the flag says: the first
67	kilobyte of one is a fragment of a frame.
68	
69	## Requests are serialised at the queue
70	
71	A `vk.Device` holds a single queue and nothing in `vk` is externally
72	synchronised, so two requests recording and submitting at once is undefined
73	behaviour rather than contention. `backend.Device` is the device plus the lock
74	that fixes that: every run and every staging pass goes through `Do`, and the
75	server is concurrent at the HTTP layer and serial at the GPU.
76	
77	That is also the only arrangement that makes sense on this part. These models
78	are each sized to saturate the iGPU; two of them interleaved would not go
79	faster, they would share a 236 GB/s bus.

82	
83	**The language model is resident, and it is most of the machine.** `-llm`
84	stages all 48 layers, the dense banks and the 512-expert bank at startup —
85	**33.5 s**, and the process then holds ~84 GB — so a request is a prefill and
86	one forward pass per token with no weight ever moving again. Two numbers are
87	decided at startup rather than per request: `-llm-ctx`, the attention cache's

89	`-llm-batch`, how many tokens the prefill arenas hold. A conversation past the
90	cache is refused with both numbers rather than truncated at one end; a prompt
91	past the batch is prefilled in chunks of it, which is the same computation by

94	**The device lock is taken per forward pass and not per request.** A
95	completion is seconds long and the speech models are milliseconds, so holding
96	the queue for a whole generation would make a transcription wait behind it for

103	once, sized for `-max-audio` seconds (60 by default), and every shorter clip
104	runs in the same arenas — `UploadMel` settles the geometry per run. A request
105	costs a front end on the host and two submits. A longer clip is refused with a
106	message saying what the server was sized for, rather than being truncated.
107	
108	**The embedding model is resident**, and it is the cheapest thing here:
109	`-embed` stages 0.88 GB of fp16 banks in **1.3 s**, and an input then costs
110	**11.5 ms** whatever it says — a 27-token query and an 8-token document take
111	the same time, because at these lengths the run is the weights read once
112	(EMBEDDING.md E6). `-embed-tokens` sizes the arenas and is therefore where an
113	input is truncated: the front of the text survives and the end-of-text token

115	truncated through it would be pooled from an ordinary word.

118	the durations decide that, so nothing can be staged until the phoneme side has

194

216	write the tool block, keep each assistant turn's `<think>`, and open the

224	space after every separator where Go's encoder writes none, and escapes
225	neither `<` nor `&` where Go escapes both, so the tool block was four

229	`</think>` from being forwarded half-written keeps the first character of a
230	stop sequence out of the stream, so a streamed answer and a buffered one are
231	the same string — the sequence itself appears in neither. They are watched in
232	the *answer* and not in the reasoning, because a `stop` of `"\n\n"` would

234	this into `finish_reason: "stop"`; Anthropic's reports `stop_sequence` and
235	says which one matched, and so does this.

238	argument raw between its tags and everything else as JSON, so rebuilding
239	`arguments` needs the tool's own parameter types: `123` is the number for an

308	worse than a refused one, because the client never learns that turning it did
309	nothing.
310	
311	## What is left
312	
313	- **Constrained decoding**, which is the one refusal above that is a missing
314	  capability rather than a missing shape. It would close `response_format`,
315	  `text.format` and a `tool_choice` that names a function in one go.
316	- **More than one conversation at a time.** The graph is one sequence's, so a
317	  second request waits — and evicts the first's reusable prefix. What would
318	  change that is a cache per conversation and the residency to hold them,
319	  which is a measurement rather than an argument.
320	- **MTP speculative decoding** (LLM.md L9), which is the next thing worth

322	- Images: `zimage/pipeline` is already the right shape for a server — resident

325	  question and not a parameter.
326	- **A forced alignment** for the transcript timings, if the 80 ms grid and the
327	  duration head's approximation ever turn out not to be enough.

layer, four of the five verticals wired to it, and the shape the fifth plugs
into.

| Endpoint | State |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/models` | **done** — lists what the process actually loaded, with the speech model's voices |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | **done** — qwen3.8-flash-next, `-llm`, buffered and SSE |
| `POST /v1/responses` | **done** — the same generation, OpenAI's newer envelope |
| `POST /v1/messages` | **done** — the same generation, Anthropic's envelope |
| `POST /v1/audio/speech` | **done** — kokoro, `-tts` |
| `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` | **done** — parakeet, `-stt`, with word and segment timings |
| `POST /v1/embeddings` | **done** — Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, `-embed`, float or base64, MRL widths |

generation prompt. A server that improvises that produces a prompt the model
has never been shown — which does not fail, it answers slightly wrong,
everywhere, with nothing to point at. So `llm.RenderChat` reproduces it, and
the acceptance criterion is Jinja's own output: `reference/dump_chat_template.py`
renders the template out of the checkpoint with the environment transformers
builds, and `TestRenderChat` diffs 23 cases character for character. The cases
that made it worth doing are the small ones — Python's `json.dumps` writes a
space after every separator where Go's encoder writes none, and escapes
neither `<` nor `&` where Go escapes both, so the tool block was four
differences away from being someone else's prompt.

**A stop sequence is another marker.** The same holdback that keeps
`</think>` from being forwarded half-written keeps the first character of a
stop sequence out of the stream, so a streamed answer and a buffered one are
the same string — the sequence itself appears in neither. They are watched in
the *answer* and not in the reasoning, because a `stop` of `"\n\n"` would
otherwise end every generation inside its own working. OpenAI's envelopes fold
this into `finish_reason: "stop"`; Anthropic's reports `stop_sequence` and
says which one matched, and so does this.

**Tool calls are read back through the schema.** The template writes a string
argument raw between its tags and everything else as JSON, so rebuilding
`arguments` needs the tool's own parameter types: `123` is the number for an
integer parameter and the text `"123"` for a string one. They are also the one
thing that is not streamed — a call is not a call until it has closed, and a
client sent half of one would have to be told to take it back.

## Transcripts have times in them

Every emission the transducer makes records the encoder frame it was made at,
and a TDT model also predicts how many frames to skip afterwards — so a word
has an end as well as a beginning without a forced alignment. `verbose_json`
reports both granularities OpenAI defines, `srt` and `vtt` are the same
segments in their two containers, and `json` stays the text alone.

Two things about them are worth stating rather than discovering. **The timings
are the model's own**: the duration head is approximate in a way a Viterbi
alignment against the audio is not, and 80 ms is the finest it can be. And
**Whisper's fields are absent rather than invented** — `avg_logprob`,
`no_speech_prob`, `compression_ratio`, `seek` and `temperature` are properties
of Whisper's decoder, and a number in them here would be a number a client
could filter on. `language` is likewise the request's or absent: this
checkpoint is multilingual and does not report which language it heard.

Words are grouped by the tokenizer's own rule (SentencePiece's U+2581 marks a
word start) and segments are sentences, which this model can do because it
punctuates — a sentence end is a token rather than a guess about silence.

## Two extensions, and three refusals

`POST /v1/embeddings` takes an **`"instruct"`** field that is not OpenAI's.
Qwen3-Embedding is instruction aware: a *query* is meant to be prefixed with a
one-sentence description of the retrieval task and a *document* is not, and
the card measures 1-5% on downstream tasks for it. There is nowhere in
OpenAI's envelope to say so, so the field carries the task description —
`"instruct": "default"` asks for the card's own — and leaving it off embeds
the text as given, which is the document behaviour and the safe half. The
prefix is applied to the *text*, so it is inside the `usage` the response
reports. `"dimensions"` is honoured the way the card asks (MRL): the vector is
truncated and renormalised, so a 32-wide vector is still a unit vector.

`POST /v1/audio/speech` takes a **`"phonemes"`** field that is not OpenAI's: IPA
to speak directly, winning over `input`. The checkpoint's vocabulary is 178 IPA
symbols and the front end that reaches them is a separate model's worth of
rules (SPEECH.md T5), so a caller that has already done that says so instead of
having it guessed. It is also how the endpoint is driven without a lexicon on
disk. `GET /v1/models` carries a **`voices`** array on the speech model, so a
client does not need a second call to populate a menu.

What is refused rather than faked:

- **`stream: true` on speech.** Kokoro decides the whole utterance's durations
  before a single sample exists, so there is nothing to send early. A whole
  body dressed as a stream would be a lie about latency.
- **`stream: true` on transcription.** The decode loop emits token by token
  and could stream, but the 40 µs submit-and-fence per emission is 38% of it
  (SPEECH.md), so what that endpoint wants is the persistent kernel, not a
  goroutine.
- **Containers other than WAV, and audio formats other than wav/pcm.**
  `audio/` is 16-bit PCM in and out on purpose. An mp3 request gets a 400
  naming what the server does encode. *Transcripts* are a different question
  and are no longer refused: `json`, `verbose_json`, `text`, `srt` and `vtt`
  all answer, because the timings they need exist.

And on the chat endpoints, the same principle with a longer list: **`n > 1`**
(n completions are n runs of a model sized to saturate the device), **`min_p`
and `repeat_penalty`** (the sampler is temperature, top_k and top_p),
**`response_format` and `text.format`** other than text, a **`tool_choice`**
that names a function, **`thinking.budget_tokens`**, and any **image content
block**. Every one of them is a 400 that says what the server
does instead. The reason is the same each time: a knob accepted and ignored is
worse than a refused one, because the client never learns that turning it did
nothing.

## What is left

- **Constrained decoding**, which is the one refusal above that is a missing
  capability rather than a missing shape. It would close `response_format`,
  `text.format` and a `tool_choice` that names a function in one go.
- **More than one conversation at a time.** The graph is one sequence's, so a
  second request waits — and evicts the first's reusable prefix. What would
  change that is a cache per conversation and the residency to hold them,
  which is a measurement rather than an argument.
- **MTP speculative decoding** (LLM.md L9), which is the next thing worth
  1.5-1.8x on the endpoint that has just been wired.
- Images: `zimage/pipeline` is already the right shape for a server — resident
  weights, `Generate(prompt, seed, progress)` — but its width and height are
  fixed at construction, so `aspect_ratio` in the request is a residency
  question and not a parameter.
- **A forced alignment** for the transcript timings, if the 80 ms grid and the
  duration head's approximation ever turn out not to be enough.

# IMAGE — the z-image-turbo vertical

> **Formed 2026-09-18, and this is now the file to read first for this
> vertical.** It supersedes [`PIPELINE.md`](PIPELINE.md), which carries a
> banner saying so and whose stage table (1-10) and validation rules remain
> the record of how the slice was built. Same rules as `LLM.md`, `SPEECH.md`
> and `EMBEDDING.md`: this file is **rewritten** each session rather than
> appended to, history goes to `TODO.md`, closed findings to `research/`.
> Stage numbers are **I0, I1, …** — the original slice's stages 1-10 keep
> their bare numbers in `research/stage-*.md` — and `§N.M` still addresses
> `IDEAS.md`.

**Target**: `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo` — prompt → PNG at up to 1024x1024, 8
steps, fp16, end to end in Go on Vulkan, served at
`POST /v1/images/generations`, with in-progress previews from
`madebyollin/taef1` (`GOALS.md`'s one line about this vertical that nothing
had scoped until now).

**Status**: **the model generates in 14.26 s, and it is served.** The kernel
work was parked 2026-09-14 with the budget below; the serving work unparked
2026-09-18: **I1** rebuilt the pipeline's geometry so width and height are a
*ceiling and a default rather than a fixed size* — every arena is sized at
construction, none of the three graphs is built for one geometry — and wired
`/v1/images/generations` with `size`, `aspect_ratio`, `seed`, `steps` and `n`
resolved at the HTTP layer (`api/images.go`, `backend.NewImage`, `-image`).
`go run ./cmd/serve -image` holds ~25 GB and answers; `-image-size 512x512`
holds a quarter of the tokens. Two refusals state their own missing pieces:
`stream: true` needs the small decoder (I2), `/v1/images/edits` needs a VAE
*encoder* (I8) — the one 501 on the server that no flag fixes.

## Where the work stands

| # | Stage | State |
|---|---|---|
| I0 | The slice: stages 1-10, prompt → PNG in **14.26 s** | **done** — `PIPELINE.md`, `research/stage-*.md` |
| I1 | Served: variable geometry + `/v1/images/generations` | **in the tree 2026-09-18** — remaining: a measured 512² image, the `API.md` row, the handoff |
| I2 | taef1 previews, and `stream: true` | open — the last capability `GOALS.md` names |
| I3 | Footprint: the five verticals in one process | open — `-llm -image` does not fit today |
| I4 | The eight elementwise passes, 1.6 s, fused into their GEMMs | open — the L2c/L2f pattern, proven since parking |
| I5 | The GEMMs' missing quarter, 2.6 s | open — two new probes since parking, no known lever |
| I6 | The VAE's elementwise fusions, ~200 ms | open |
| I7 | Attention's last 1.1x, ~0.2 s | parked — register-bound, twice measured |
| I8 | `/v1/images/edits`: the VAE encoder, and whether at all | decision first — see below |

The order is deliberate: **capabilities before percents** (the same argument
that parked this vertical for the speech ones), and I3 before the kernel work
because serving all five models at once is `GOALS.md`'s actual last line.

## The model, as the checkpoint describes it

`go run ./cmd/inspect models/Z-Image-Turbo/<part>`; full table in
`PIPELINE.md`. What the open items rest on:

| | |
|---|---|
| DiT | **34** blocks (30 `layers` + 2 context + 2 noise refiners), dim 3840, 30 heads of 128, SwiGLU 10240, adaLN `[15360, 256]` |
| Weights, fp16 | text encoder (Qwen3-4B) **7.07 GB**, transformer **12.54 GB**, VAE 0.30 GB, activations 4.90 GB — ~25 GB resident, 21.9 s to load |
| Geometry | 16-ch latents, patch 2 → both sides a multiple of **16**; 1024² is 4096 image tokens, 512² is 1024 |
| Schedule | FlowMatchEuler, shift 3.0, **8 NFE** (a turbo distillation — `steps` is a knob for looking at the trade, not tuning) |
| Weight sizes vs the 32 MiB MALL | attention projections 3840² fp16 = **29.5 MB, under it**; the three FFN matrices 78.6 MB, **over it** (I5) |

## Where the image budget stands

`go run ./cmd/zimage -width 1024`, two runs to 14.18/14.34 s. Unchanged since
stage 10; I1 moved no arithmetic.

| | per image, 1024², 8 steps | share |
|---|---|---|
| the 34 DiT blocks | 13.3 s | 93.1% |
| — of which the seven projections | **9.9 s** at 73-76% of the WMMA ceiling | 69% |
| — of which attention | 1.9 s at 38 TFLOP/s | 13% |
| — of which eight elementwise passes | 1.6 s | 11% |
| VAE decode | 0.81 s | 5.7% |
| text encoder + host + refiners | 0.15 s | 1.0% |
| **total** | **14.26 s** | |

Per step there is also a **~50 ms remainder no dispatch accounts for** (wall
1.67-1.70 s against 1.66 s of timestamps; stage 9 ruled out submit batching).
L7d built the tool that would attribute it: a timestamp after *every*
dispatch, which is also what llama.cpp's perf logger reports.

## The hypotheses, re-checked (2026-09-18)

Four sessions of parking and forty of LLM/speech work later, what this
vertical believed:

1. **"`aspect_ratio` is a residency question, not a parameter"** (`API.md`) —
   **disproven, constructively**: I1 made size a per-request parameter under a
   token ceiling, the same arrangement `-max-audio` gives parakeet. What the
   arenas bound is the *token count*, so a server built for 1024² also runs
   512x2048 and refuses 1024x1088 (`ImageGeometry.MaxPixels`).
2. **"Do not quantize the DiT for speed"** (§3.4) — **still true at every
   servable size**: intensity is `4*M` flop/byte against the 235 crossover,
   and even 512² (M=1024) is 4096. But the *reason to quantize changed*: it
   was "footprint only, someday", and I3 makes footprint the blocker for
   `GOALS.md`. Meanwhile `LLM.md` built the entire toolchain — L8a's staging
   of Q8 as int8 + fp16 scales unpacked into LDS per K-step, §2.8-tiled, with
   the checkpoint's own (d, q) recovered exactly — and §0 says int8 WMMA runs
   at fp16 rate, so on a compute-bound DiT, Q8 should be **speed-neutral**.
3. **"The missing GEMM quarter is the top item"** (stage 10's parting
   ranking) — **demoted, deliberately**. It is still the biggest number
   (2.6 s), but the ablation behind `results/gemm_wmma.csv` is 1.25x *behind*
   what the pipeline already does — no known lever — while the elementwise
   fusions (I4) now have a proven pattern: L2c consumed a 21 MB SwiGLU gate
   inside the up projection's epilogue so the tensor was never written, and
   L2f fused two norms, two ropes and the tiling into one pass. Ranked by
   size the quarter wins; ranked by expected value it no longer does.
4. **The error margin is thinner than it looks.** End to end against
   diffusers at 256² the pipeline sits at **2.2e-2 of a 3e-2 bound** — stage
   10 alone ate a third of the margin, as a chaotic trajectory landing
   elsewhere rather than an accuracy loss. Anything that perturbs an operand
   (I3 above all) re-runs `reference/dump_zimage_run.py`'s composition first,
   and should expect to need the bound re-derived the way L8c had to build
   its own perplexity grade — a trajectory that lands elsewhere is not wrong,
   and the test that can say so does not exist yet.
5. **One kernel wins all three DiT shapes** (stage 4) — **measured at M=4096
   only**. Variable size makes M=1152 a real workload; still compute-bound,
   but `cmd/ditstack -image 1024` is one run and `qwen.PlanFor` is the
   precedent if the answer moves.

## The open stages

**I2 — taef1 previews.** OpenAI's streaming image endpoint sends partial
images as the denoiser goes; the pipeline already calls `Progress(Step)` after
every step and `Request.Latents`/`GenerateFrom` already exist. What is missing
is only the decoder: the full VAE costs 0.81 s against a 1.7 s step, so a
preview through it would cost half the image, and taef1 is the same 16-channel
Flux latent space at roughly a hundredth of the VAE's size — stage 8's conv
kernels should put it in the low milliseconds. The oracle is diffusers'
`AutoencoderTiny` (the established dump pattern), and the dump decides the
scale/shift convention rather than the model card. Then `stream: true` answers
with `partial_image` events and the refusal comes out.

**I3 — footprint.** `-llm` is 79.85 GB and `-image` ~25; today they are
separate processes. Q8 on the encoder and the DiT is ~11 GB off (both
compute-bound where it matters — the encoder is memory-bound but 0.4% of an
image), 4.5 bits on the DiT would be ~9 GB more if the composition tolerates
it. Whether the five verticals then fit in one process is a measurement, not
an argument — and it is gated on hypothesis 4's test existing.

**I4 — the elementwise passes.** Eight passes, 5.93 ms a block, 1.6 s an
image, each reading the residual stream and writing it. `swiglu` (1.45 ms) is
L2c's gate trick verbatim; the two tanh-gated residuals (0.89, 0.85) belong in
the epilogues of `to_out` and `w2`; the adaLN scales in the norms. Not all of
1.6 s comes out — the norms still have to read the stream — but the pattern
is proven and the bandwidth arithmetic (stage 10's exactness: bytes removed =
time returned) prices each fusion before it is written.

**I5 — the missing quarter.** Two probes that did not exist at parking: L2f
found the *same kernel* wanting opposite BM schedules on weights either side
of the 32 MiB MALL, and this DiT straddles it (table above) while running one
schedule for everything; and L7d's per-dispatch timestamps would finally
attribute the ~50 ms/step remainder, which is 0.4 s an image on its own.
Neither is promised more than ~1.05x; both are cheap to ask.

**I6 — the VAE's fusions.** 63% of the decode is bandwidth-bound elementwise
back to back over the same tensors; a SiLU whose only consumer is a conv can
write the blocked fp16 form instead of its fp32 output. ~200 ms, 1.4%.

**I8 — edits.** A decision before any code: `GOALS.md` does not ask for
edits — the endpoint exists because OpenAI's surface does. If wanted, the
cheap path is the Flux VAE *encoder* (34 M params, stage-8 machinery plus
stride-2 convs) feeding `GenerateFrom` SDEdit-style — noise the encoded
latent to an intermediate step, run the rest. Whether a turbo distillation
edits acceptably at 8 NFE is exactly the kind of thing the 256² composition

# IMAGE — the z-image-turbo vertical

> **Formed 2026-09-18, and this is now the file to read first for this
> vertical.** It supersedes [`PIPELINE.md`](PIPELINE.md), which carries a
> banner saying so and whose stage table (1-10) and validation rules remain
